q: 1. The edge of drawing board where T-square is made to slide is called
explain: The working edge (or ebony edge) is a perfectly straight wooden strip on the left side of the drawing board used to guide the T-square.

q: 2. The needle point of the compass should be…… the lead point.
explain: The needle point must be slightly longer than the pencil lead so the needle penetrates the paper while the lead still touches the surface to draw the arc.

q: 3. As per ISI recommended size of drawing board is/are
explain: ISI (Indian Standards Institution) specifies these standard sizes for drawing boards to ensure uniformity in technical drawings.

q: 4. Working edge of drawing board is kept ........... of the user.
explain: For right-handed users, the ebony/working edge is always on the left so the T-square can be manipulated by the left hand while drawing with the right.

q: 5. Drawing board is made of
explain: Softwood like white pine or fir is used because it allows drawing pins to be inserted and removed easily, and 'seasoning' prevents warping.

q: 6. Drawing equipment used by draftsmen primarily as a guide for drawing horizontal lines on a drafting table is
explain: The T-square's blade slides along the working edge of the drawing board, providing a reliable guide for drawing horizontal lines.

q: 7. The working edge of T-square is used to
options: as a base of set square
explain: The T-square serves multiple purposes: drawing horizontal lines, ensuring they are parallel, and providing a base for set squares to draw vertical or inclined lines.

q: 8. Set squares are not used to draw
explain: Horizontal lines are primarily drawn using the T-square or a mini-drafter; set squares are typically used for vertical and inclined lines relative to the T-square.

q: 9. To prevent warping of the board ........are cleated at its back.
explain: Battens are wooden strips fixed to the back of the board to prevent it from bending or warping due to moisture or temperature changes.

q: 10. The two parts of T-square are........ and .......
explain: A T-square consists of a 'stock' (the head) and a 'blade' (the long straight edge) joined at a $90^{\circ}$ angle.

q: 11. Angles in multiples of 15 degrees are constructed by the combined use of
explain: By combining $45^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}/60^{\circ}$ set squares on a T-square base, one can achieve angles like $15^{\circ}$, $75^{\circ}$, $105^{\circ}$, etc.

q: 12. To draw or measure angles ........... is used.
explain: A protractor is specifically designed with degree graduations to measure and mark angles accurately.

q: 13. For drawing large-size circles .................. is attached to the compass (>150mm).
explain: A lengthening bar is an extension that increases the radius of the compass beyond its standard limit.

q: 14. Circles of small radii are drawn by means of a
explain: Bow compasses are rigid and small, making them ideal for maintaining precision while drawing small circles.

q: 15. .......... is used for setting of short equal distances.
explain: Bow dividers are used for repeating small, equal measurements along a line accurately.

q: 16. In drafting machine, which one does not follow
explain: A drafting machine (mini-drafter) combines the functions of a T-square, set squares, and protractor, but has nothing to do with leveling equipment.

q: 17. Which one is not drafting equipment?
explain: All listed items (drafter, scale, and even a dust cloth to keep the sheet clean) are considered part of the drafting environment.

q: 18. Circles of very small radii are drawn by means of a
explain: A drop compass is specifically used for very tiny circles, where the center point remains fixed while the pencil lead 'drops' and rotates around it.

q: 19. .............is used to protect the adjoining lines on the drawing when some parts of the line is being erased.
explain: An erasing shield is a thin metal or plastic plate with holes of various shapes that allows erasing a specific area without disturbing nearby lines.

q: 20. For drawing thin lines of uniform thickness the pencil should be sharpened in the form of -
explain: A chisel edge is used for drawing long, thin, uniform lines (like outlines) because the wide edge wears down more slowly than a point.

q: 21. Which of the following is attached to the compass used to draw large size circle
explain: A lengthening bar is fitted to a compass leg to extend its reach for drawing circles of large radius.

q: 22. Parallel ruling straight edge machine is used to draw
explain: A parallel ruling straight-edge is a drafting machine attachment that slides vertically on wires/cords while remaining horizontal, used primarily to draw horizontal parallel lines.

q: 23. ......... is used for drawing curves which can't be drawn by a compass
explain: French curves are templates with various irregular radii used to draw smooth, non-circular curves.

q: 24. To remove unnecessary lines ....... is used
explain: The standard tool for correcting errors or removing construction lines is an eraser.

q: 25. Uses of the T-square, set squares, scale and protractor are combined in the
explain: A drafting machine (or mini-drafter) is an all-in-one tool that replaces several individual drafting instruments.

q: 26. Circle and arcs of circles are drawn by means of a .......
explain: A compass is the primary instrument used for drawing circular geometry.

q: 27. Inking pen is used for drawing ----------- in ink
explain: While technical pens can be used for many things, traditional inking pens were primarily used with guides to draw permanent straight lines.

q: 28. The edge of the board on which T-square is made to slide is called .............
explain: The left (or designated) straight edge of the drawing board, along which the T-square's stock slides, is called the working edge.

q: 29. Set squares are used for drawing ......., ......... and .......... lines.
explain: Set squares are versatile tools used to draw vertical lines, standard angles (30, 45, 60), and parallel lines when slid along a reference.

q: 30. A drafter helps in drawing .............
explain: A drafter (drafting machine) is designed mainly to draw parallel and perpendicular lines quickly and accurately using its scale arms set at fixed angles.

q: 31. Set squares are used to draw
explain: Used alone or with a T-square, set squares can draw vertical lines, inclined lines at fixed angles, and sets of parallel lines.

q: 32. For dimensioning and lettering normally following pencils are used
explain: H is used for thin, precise dimension lines, and HB is used for lettering to make it clear and legible.

q: 33. Which of the following pencil leads is hardest?
explain: On the pencil grading scale, 'H' denotes hardness (higher H numbers = harder); among HB, H, B, F, the H grade is the hardest listed.

q: 34. The most important material for drawing is
explain: Without paper and a marking tool (pencil), no drawing can be created; they are the fundamental necessities.

q: 35. To lay off an angle from a given line, what marks on the protractor should you align for a higher accuracy?
explain: For accurate angle layout, the protractor's center mark must be aligned with the vertex of the angle, and the 0°–180° baseline aligned with the reference line, so all three (0°, 180°, and center) marks are used together.

q: 36. The most important material for drawing is
explain: Paper (the drawing surface) and pencil (the marking tool) are the two most basic and essential materials for any drawing.

q: 37. Which pencil is used for thinner line ?
explain: The 'H' stands for Hardness. Higher numbers (like 2H) have harder lead, which produces thinner, lighter lines.

q: 38. To draw smooth curves of any nature, drafting instrument used is .............
explain: A French curve is a flexible-shaped template specifically designed to help draw smooth irregular curves that are not simple arcs of a circle.

q: 39. 9H pencil is ......than the 7H pencil
explain: In the pencil grading system, 9H is the hardest grade available, making it harder than 7H.

q: 40. Parallel lines can be drawn with the help of .............
explain: Parallel lines can be drawn using a mini-drafter, a T-square (sliding along the board edge), or a pair of set squares (one sliding against the other), so all listed tools work.

q: 41. To draw very light line which pencil is used
explain: Harder pencils (like 2H) do not deposit much graphite, resulting in very light construction lines.

q: 42. Extension arm used with engineering compass facilitates .............
options: to draw circles of larger diameter
to adjust distance between the legs
explain: An extension (lengthening) bar attached to a compass increases its radius reach, allowing the drafter to draw circles of larger diameter than the compass alone permits.

q: 43. The equipment mainly used to transfer the measurements is
explain: Dividers have two sharp points specifically intended to pick up distances from a scale and transfer them to the work without marking the original source.

q: 44. Stock of T-square makes an angle with working edge
explain: The stock is fixed perpendicular (90°) to the blade so it registers squarely against the board's working edge.

q: 45. The hardness of the pencil lead increase as numeral letter H
explain: In the pencil grading scale, a higher number before 'H' (e.g., 4H vs 2H) indicates a harder, lighter lead.

q: 46. A letter B in any pencil denotes .............
explain: In the pencil grading system, 'B' stands for blackness/softness of the lead — higher B numbers indicate softer, darker leads, as opposed to 'H' which denotes hardness.

q: 47. The needle point of the compass should be .......than the lead point
explain: The needle point is set slightly longer so it stays anchored in the paper while the lead point traces the circle.

q: 48. Parallel ruling straight edge machine is used to draw
explain: The parallel ruling straight edge slides vertically on the board to draw a series of accurate horizontal lines.

q: 49. Set squares are not used to draw .............
explain: Set squares, being rigid triangular tools with fixed straight edges, are used for straight and standard-angle lines but cannot be used to draw irregular curves — that requires a French curve.

q: 50. The diameter of semi-circle is called .............
explain: A protractor's semicircular scale has its straight diametrical edge referred to as the base of the protractor.
